checksPerformed.description: every depth-1 authority (proxyAdmin, owner, each AccessControl role) was resolved to its terminal controller and checked for a delay; the protocol window is the minimum across them
checksPerformed.note: 1 route(s) enumerated; none was found to impose zero delay

checksPerformed.description: each detected timelock's own dispatcher was searched for updateDelay(uint256)/setDelay(uint256) — i.e. whether the delay is mutable at all
where a delay mutator exists, it was probed by eth_call from three unrelated addresses and the revert read: a self-call gate proves the delay binds itself; a role gate proves it does not
each detected timelock was checked for being itself behind a proxy — a delay enforced by replaceable code binds only as strongly as the authority over that code
cancellers/executors on a detected timelock were considered and are modelled as NOT window-shortening: cancelling removes a queued change rather than making one arrive sooner
checksPerformed.note: by construction a canceller cannot shorten a delay; an emergency PAUSE is a different power and is modelled on the time-to-exit side (it blocks the exit, it does not shorten the notice)

checksPerformed.description: pendingOwner authorities were excluded from the route set: a pending owner holds no power until it accepts, so counting it would inflate the window's route set with an authority that cannot currently act
whether a governance contract on the path can queue an arbitrary call that reaches the target by some route other than the ones enumerated here
checksPerformed.note: NOT CHECKED. Enumerating what an arbitrary-call governor can reach requires modelling proposal execution, which is out of scope. Where a governor sits behind a timelock the delay still applies to it, so this gap does not make a reported delay optimistic; where a governor is reachable WITHOUT a delay it is already captured as an ungated route.

checksPerformed.description: whether a Safe on the path has modules or a guard that could let a subset of signers (or a non-signer) act
checksPerformed.note: NOT CHECKED. Safe modules are not enumerated. This does not affect the window arithmetic, because a Safe is already modelled as imposing ZERO notice — a module could change WHO acts, not HOW FAST.

liquidity.reason: Liquidity depth is not modelled. Establishing whether a given position could actually be sold requires pool discovery and depth integration across venues — an indexer, which Ripcord deliberately does not run (same reason its major-token list is curated). Any shortcut available here would produce an authoritative-looking number that is not one, so no number is produced. Practical consequence: for a position large relative to available liquidity the real time-to-exit is LONGER than the figure above, never shorter.

timeToExit.statement: No exit-delay mechanism was detected: none of the cooldown/unstaking accessors Ripcord knows resolve, and no two-step request/claim exit shape is present in the dispatcher. Exit appears to be synchronous. This is a positive observation over a curated, finite pattern table — not proof that no delay exists.
